nonvacuity: Unconditional explicit witness, with no implication premises. The base mass is q(k)=2^(-(k+1)); sum q=1 by the geometric series. For every n>=2, 0<n^(-3)<1, so mixMass n is a genuine mixture of q and its integer translate, with positive mass at every nonnegative integer and finite moments of every order. Denominators in the asserted mean quotient are strictly positive. Natural subtraction in the shifted component is guarded by n<=k.

Take a countable product of N(0,1) and coordinate projections X_i. Then X_0 is in L2 with variance 1>0, and all IID premises hold. The generic countable-product IID construction, including the coordinate pushforward law, was kernel-checked in scratch/Check.lean. The second conjunct is the unconditional finite-moment geometric witness of T1.

The actual witness law is nondegenerate: its X density is 1/2 on two intervals of total length 2, and its independent Y density is 1/2 on an interval of length 2. Their product has mass 1, bounded coordinates and mean X=0. The CEF zero and the globally C1 bump agree everywhere on positive support but have derivatives 0 and 1 at 0; scaling the bump gives every real derivative. No inconsistent antecedent or derivative default is used.

Take K=1, X uniform on [-1,1], Y identically zero, U=(-1,1), f=1/2 on [-1,1] and zero elsewhere, m=mprime=0, coordinate k=0 and a=0. X is measurable and integrable, f is a true vector density positive on U, EX=0 belongs to U, both CEFs are globally measurable and integrable, and the asserted antecedent is an actual derivative. This is a positive-dimensional instance.

Use the countable product of Uniform[0,1] x N(0,1), with its two coordinate projections at each time. At every finite design, a least-squares minimizer exists by projection onto the finite-dimensional column space; choose the minimum coefficient-norm minimizer, including fit=0 at n=0. This selection is measurable on matrix rank strata. With continuous iid X, all design points are distinct almost surely, and for n>=2 the degree is below n, so the fit is unique almost surely. The supplied-fit premises are jointly satisfiable; arbitrary choices on singular null designs do not affect the outer probabilities in the liminf. Compact polynomial-square integrals are finite. The general IID product construction was kernel-checked.

For the consistency clause, take iid Uniform[0,1] covariates, Y=0, m=0, V=0, fit=0, normalized shifted Legendre polynomials, J_n=floor(n^(1/4)), and c=1/2. Then J_n tends to infinity, (J_n+1)/n tends to zero, and the row-envelope bound sum p_k(x)^2<=(J_n+1)^2 gives E||G_n-I||_F^2<=((J_n+1)^3-(J_n+1))/n, hence the required Gram event probability tends to one by Markov. Thus hgram is not being assumed without an instance. The same law and basis with J_n=0, zeta2_n=1 satisfy the separate general-envelope and uniform-cubic clauses. The finite-bound clause has the nonempty case K=n=1, p_0=1. All integrals are over bounded support, and K>0 makes gramDeviation a nonempty finite supremum.

Take the countable product of the four explicitly positive atom masses 3/8,1/8,1/8,3/8. All observations are binary, the parameter interval [1/10,9/10] is nonempty, and the sample has an attained unique clipped MLE for every positive sample size. For the second clause choose q=1/2, or any q in (0,1); both conditioning probabilities are then positive. Bernoulli likelihood and KL logarithm denominators stay strictly positive. The general IID product construction was kernel-checked.

Use positive dimensions K=tau=1, constant covariate X=0 with nuX=delta_0, kappa=delta_0+delta_1 on outcomes, true f(y,x)=1/2 on {0,1}, and g(y,x,t)=t_0 on y=1 and 1-t_0 on y=0 (zero elsewhere). Take Theta=[1/4,3/4], tstar=1/2, iid fair binary outcomes and that_n=clip_[1/4,3/4](sample mean). This is a nondegenerate identified model, not an empty parameter set. M(t)=(log t+log(1-t))/2 is separated and uniformly bounded; all entropy and cross-entropy integrals are genuine finite sums. For n>0 take Delta_n=|sampleMean-1/2| log 3, Delta_0=log 4, and e_n=0. The required pointwise bounds hold, Delta tends to zero by the LLN, and the clipped mean maximizes likelihood. The compactness clause can also use this same interval, and the true-model clause the same family. scratch/Check.lean proves directly that the sample-zero envelope implies the uniform population bound. Revision 2: take commonS={(x,y): y=0 or y=1}. It is measurable and has probability one under the true observation law; for all parameters t in [1/4,3/4], both conditional masses t and 1-t are strictly positive on this same set. scratch/DeltaCheck.lean kernel-checks this positive-dimensional common-set instance, normalization against delta_0+delta_1, and a fair observation law with both cells of mass 1/2. It also proves from the actual new common-set hypotheses that, almost surely, all countably many observations have positive density simultaneously for every fitted parameter, and verifies log(sampleLikelihood)=n*sampleLogLikelihood on positive samples. Thus the parameter-dependent log(0)=0 defect is fixed. The n=0 finite-envelope restriction remains disclosed.

Unconditional, with the actual nonempty sample (1,2,3). For example sigma=1 makes (1/2,1/4,1,sigma,0,1,1) admissible; the same path for all sigma>0 has strictly positive scales, weights and rate. The normal contribution at y=1 grows like 1/sigma, while positive exponential contributions bound the other two factors away from zero. Every admissible parameter gives finite likelihood.

For the first clause choose n=1 and y_0=1. For the restricted clause choose B=1,S=2,delta=1,a=1,b=2; the vector (1/2,1/4,0,1,0,1,1) belongs to the restriction with strictly positive component weights and scales. This membership was kernel-checked in scratch/Check.lean. The nonempty compact set has positive scale and rate lower bounds, so no division-by-zero convention gives the attainment result.

There are actual distinct parameters theta_A=(1,1/3,1/4) and theta_B=(1,1/3,3/4) in the three-dimensional parameter box, and their actual observed probabilities are (2/3,1/3,0,0), normalized and nonnegative. Parameter membership, distinctness, equality of the two mass vectors, and total mass one were kernel-checked in scratch/Check.lean. For every positive n the sample space has 4^n elements and the observed experiment is not empty; a compact continuous likelihood has a maximizer. The zero component is exactly the claimed nonidentification.

Nonidentification has a positive-dimensional instance using the two disjoint four-outcome components from T11, M=2, tau=3, K=1 with constant covariate, kappa the sum of Dirac masses at 0,1,2,3, and the two distinct zero-weight-boundary parameters. Expected log likelihood is integrable on the two-point observed support. For both consistency and normality/efficiency take M=1, weight=1, K=tau=1, constant X=0, kappa=delta_0+delta_1, g_t(1)=t and g_t(0)=1-t, Theta=[1/4,3/4], theta=1/2, delta=1/8 and iid fair binary outcomes. Let S be the two supported observations and use the clipped sample mean as the measurable global MLE (at n=0 any parameter maximizes). The score is +/-2, I=4 is positive definite, the expected Hessian is -1/(2t^2)-1/(2(1-t)^2), continuous with value -4 at theta. For n>0 the log error envelope is |sampleMean-1/2| log 3 and a Hessian envelope on the stated ball is 16|sampleMean-1/2|; set the n=0 envelopes to log 4 and 16 respectively. Both converge to zero by the LLN. The finite-support square-root family is differentiable in quadratic mean with genuinely integrable squared remainders. These are independent-coordinate, nonzero-dimensional hypotheses; they do not assume MLE consistency or its limit law. The competing RegularAL class is nonempty: the untruncated binary sample mean has influence Y-1/2 and local-alternative variance 1/4. Revision 2: the standalone compact-consistency clause additionally uses the same measurable commonS={(x,y): y=0 or y=1} for the one-component Bernoulli mixture with weight one and success parameter in [1/4,3/4]. This has true probability one and every fitted mixture density is strictly positive on it. The new premises are jointly satisfiable with all the previously described positive-dimensional Bernoulli assumptions. scratch/DeltaCheck.lean verifies the common-set instance, conditional normalization, simultaneous positivity for all observations and fitted parameters, the positive log-product identity, and exclusion of the diagonal-zero countermodel. The normality/efficiency clause already contained a common set and is unchanged; the sample-zero envelopes, joint QMD premise and local remainder-integrability restriction remain disclosed.

The density matchingUnitLaw integrates to 1: summing over response flags gives 1, summing over the two noise flags gives 2, and the score interval has length 1/2. Take its countable iid product. The scores are continuously distributed on [1/4,3/4], and signs are independent and fair. For every finite sample hotDeck lies in [49,51], including its no-respondent fallback; bootVar is bounded by 4. Tie ambiguities between distinct original donors occur on null sets; duplicate bootstrap donors have identical outcomes, so the statistic and bootstrap variance have measurable versions and satisfy all the added per-n L2 premises. The IID product construction was kernel-checked; the long Poisson occupancy asymptotics were not independently re-proved.

Use the same nondegenerate iid matchingUnitLaw product as T13; hotDeck and its bootstrap variance have bounded measurable versions and all added L2 premises hold. The deterministic conditional-variance clause is already nontrivial at n=1 with r_0=true: hotDeck=50+noise, donorReuseWeight=1 and conditional variance 1. It also handles r identically false with hotDeck=50, weights zero and variance zero; this fallback is deliberate, not the only satisfiable case.

Take the nondegenerate countable iid product of matchingUnitLaw. Interpret X=P-1/4, Y(0)=noise, Y(1)=0. causalMatch is bounded by 1 in absolute value and its bootstrap variance by 4; both have measurable versions, as ties between distinct original donor scores occur only on null sets and duplicate donors share outcomes. Thus the L2 premises hold at every n. E[D-(P-1/4)]=1/4 and bounded iid sampling makes the clipped intercept consistent. This instance has real controls and treated units with positive probabilities; it does not exploit an empty donor population.

Use the same nondegenerate product law as T15. A common translation of every score leaves the entire minimizer predicate unchanged, including ties; hence the classical-choice nearestDonor selection, causalMatch and every resampled statistic coincide. The estimated statistic and bootstrap variance therefore have the same bounded measurable versions and satisfy all L2 premises. In the deterministic variance clause choose n=1 and d_0=false: the statistic is -noise with variance 1, so that clause has a nonzero instance as well as the explicitly defined no-control fallback.

Every one of the 12 placeboLaw cells is strictly positive, the weights sum to 1, and the treatment probabilities at X=-1,0,1 are 3/4,1/4,3/4. Positivity of all cells and the two exact population risks were kernel-checked in scratch/Check.lean. Take its countable iid product for the asymptotic clause, using the checked generic IID construction. The full regressor moment matrix is [[1,0,2/3],[0,2/3,0],[2/3,0,11/12]], determinant 17/54, and both limiting residual risks are positive; sample singularities therefore disappear almost surely eventually. Exact fraction arithmetic in scratch/exact-arithmetic.json independently gives HC0 asymptotic variance 135315/334084, scaled Wald limit 18496/135315, scaled F limit 64/531 and the displayed risk-based 240 value 5056/177. Standard F quantiles exist for every alpha in (0,1), so the rejection clause is not an empty critical-value implication.

A positive-dimensional instance is K=L=1 with independent fair Rademacher X,W and independent Bernoulli(1/2) D on eight equally likely atoms. Take gamma=(1/2,0). Conditional independence and the linear CEF hold, all second moments are finite, both treatment values have positive probability, and the moment matrix of (1,X,W) is the identity, so the rank premise holds. The separate failure-without-linearity conjunct uses the actual positive twelve-cell placebo law and its nonzero coefficient 4/17, independently checked via exact risks.

Unconditional explicit countable probability law: assign joint mass 3^(-(k+1)) to (X=k+1,D=1) and 2^(-(k+2)) to (X=k+1,D=0). Geometric series give respective totals (1/3)/(1-1/3)=1/2 and (1/4)/(1-1/2)=1/2. Every joint cell is strictly positive, so conditioning denominators are nonzero and both arm supports are exactly the positive integers. Positivity and interior propensities for arbitrary k were kernel-checked in scratch/Check.lean. The formula e_k=2/(2+(3/2)^(k+1)) tends to zero; no empty support or null cell produces the failure of a uniform margin.
